proposedBy: Codex, implementing the LLP 0063 Step 4 remediation
ratifier: Charlie Cheever, as named by partitime.comparison-protocol.v1

replacement.scope: All twelve web/build cells rerun prospectively under the unchanged workload, sampling counts, formulas, hardware profile, and holdout isolation. The old artifacts remain historical and cannot validate v2.
replacement.warmPrimeRule: Prime the same cell in a sibling browser target, close that target, then measure in a fresh target in the same browser profile. This preserves the shared warm HTTP cache without retaining a second application document in the measured target's back/forward cache.
replacement.thresholdPolicy: Recompute every v2 threshold from the rerun React controls using the already-ratified formulas. Corrected values may move in either direction; equality continues to pass.

cause.finding: The v1 collector performed the cache-prime navigation in the measurement target and then navigated that target again. Chrome retained the priming document in back/forward cache, while Runtime.getHeapUsage covered the target heap. The metric declared one active page and one logical subscription but included retained state from two application documents.
cause.notAProductOptimization: The correction changes target custody only. It does not disable bfcache, change application lifecycle behavior, alter polling cadence, remove a feature, or loosen a formula.

correctedDiagnostic.interpretation: The diagnostic is not a replacement calibration. It isolates the custody correction: cold and warm heaps converge for all three arms once the priming target is closed.
